text:
rebecca: noticing a cluster of duplicate streaming charges from us-west after the proxy pool change. console alarmed on streaming-heartbeat for several tenants :frowning_face:
oscar: which change did we roll? I think we tightened keepalive and shortened idle_close in yesterday's canary
rebecca: correct. idle_close moved 50s->20s. traces show proxy sending RST/half-close, client retries with same resume token, runtime sometimes creates a new billable session
rebecca: small trace:
```
[proxy] 2026-03-24T08:12:01Z conn=abcd action=RST_SENT idle_close=20s host=px-12
[client] 2026-03-24T08:12:02Z reconnect resume_id=r-332 fp=sha256:xx
[runtime] 2026-03-24T08:12:02Z resume=r-332 result=stale -> new_session billable=true
```
kyle: SDKs differ: some treat RST as terminal and drop resume context, others attempt resume. Combined with aggressive socket churn we get overlapping sessions for same resume_id
sonya: ops: quickest stopgap is console alert dedupe for affected tenant set. longer-term: runtime should accept reattach when fingerprint matches (non-billable) and we can flag proxy to avoid hard RST if resume token exists
oscar: agree. options: 1) runtime idempotent-attach on fingerprint match (needs audit + billing reconciliation), 2) proxy FF to suppress RST when resume header present, 3) console-level dedupe window to mute alerts during rollout
rebecca: propose combo: small runtime canary for idempotent attach gated by FF, proxy FF to suppress RST at 10% initially, and console dedupe 30s for streaming-heartbeat alerts
kyle: runtime pseudo: ```python
def handle_resume(req):
    tok = req.headers.get('x-resume')
    if token_store.exists(tok) and fingerprint_ok(req):
        metrics.incr('resume.reattach')
        audit.log('reattach', tok, req.fp)
        return attach_existing(tok)  # non-billable
    return create_session(req)  # billable
```
sonya: make sure token lookup is constant time and add guardrails so old tokens can't be reattached. also add audit event for billing team to retro-dedupe if needed
deploy-bot: deploy requested: canary/runtime/reattach-idempotent -> queued on eng-runtime-canary
oscar: timeline: land runtime canary in ~30m, enable proxy FF at 10% after runtime canary is green, monitor metrics: resume.reattach, billing.delta, active_sockets_per_resume. if anything odd, rollback FF and revert proxy change
rebecca: I'll notify CS and pin an incident note in console. Thanks team — will update after canary run :thumbsup:
